title: PERIODIC LABOUR FORCE SURVEY (PLFS) Quarterly Bulletin April – June, 2026
subtitle:
Male LFPR in urban areas increased
Urban UR remained stable
Secondary sector employment recorded an increase in both rural and urban areas
Regular wage/ salaried employees witnessed a rise
body_text:
Snapshots of Quarterly Bulletin of  PLFS April to June 2026: · The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above was 54.6% during April–June 2026 , compared to 55.5% in the previous quarter. · The urban LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above remained unchanged at 50.2% during April–June 2026 . · The male LFPR (15 years and above) in urban areas increased marginally to 75.3% in April–June 2026 , from 75.0% in the previous quarter. · The urban Worker Population Ratio (WPR) for persons aged 15 years and above remained stable at 46.8% during April–June 2026 . · The share of regular wage/salaried employees among persons aged 15 years and above increased in both rural and urban areas, rising from 15.5% to 16.1% in rural areas and from 48.9% to 49.3% in urban areas. · The share of employment in the secondary sector for persons aged 15 years and above increased in both rural and urban areas during April–June 2026 . · The share of employment in the tertiary sector for persons aged 15 years and above recorded an increase in rural areas during April–June 2026 . · The urban Unemployment Rate (UR) for persons aged 15 years and above remained broadly stable at 6.7% during April–June 2026 .
Introduction The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment-unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework. Considering the need to generate high-frequency labour force indicators with wider coverage, the sampling methodology of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was revamped from January, 2025. The redesigned PLFS aims to achieve the following objectives: To generate key employment and unemployment indicators – namely Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) – every month for both rural and urban areas at the all-India level under the Current Weekly Status (CWS). To extend the Quarterly PLFS results to rural areas, thereby producing quarterly estimates of labour market indicators for both rural and urban India under the CWS framework. To provide annual estimates of key employment and unemployment indicators in both Usual Status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status (CWS) for rural as well as urban areas. Earlier PLFS Quarterly Bulletins released up to December, 2024, presented labour market indicators only for urban areas. The Bulletin for April – June, 2025 marked the first in the series to provide estimates for both rural and urban areas and the current Bulletin for April – June, 2026 is the fifth in the series. In this Quarterly Bulletin , efforts have been made to provide estimates of the number of workers in absolute terms . This Quarterly Bulletin presents estimates of key labour force indicators — Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Unemployment Rate (UR), and the distribution of workers by broad employment status and industry of work — in the Current Weekly Status (CWS), separately for rural and urban areas at the all-India level. In addition, state-level estimates of LFPR, WPR, and UR in CWS are also provided for selected States . Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS: Urban Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) remained unchanged: Overall LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above stood at 54.6% in the quarter April-June, 2026 as compared to 55.5% observed in the previous quarter. Rural LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above observed as 56.9% in the current quarter compared with 58.2% in the previous quarter. LFPR for persons aged 15 years and above in urban areas remained unchanged compared to the last quarter. Overall female LFPR stood at 33.2% during the current quarter compared to 34.7% in the previous quarter. The male LFPR in urban areas witnessed a marginal increase to 75.3% during the quarter from 75.0% observed in the quarter January-March, 2026. The overall LFPR during the quarter April-June, 2026 registered a modest fall of 0.4 percentage points compared to April-June, 2025. Rural LFPR is almost stable at 56.9% during the current quarter compared to 57.1% recorded during the same quarter of 2025, while the urban LFPR experienced a decrease of 0.4 percentage points. Urban LFPR for persons of age 15 years and above remains unchanged at 50.2% in April-June, 2026. Urban workforce maintains stability: Overall Worker Population Ratio (WPR) for persons of age 15 years and above estimated at 51.7% during the quarter April-June, 2026 compared to 52.8% in the previous quarter. Urban WPR for persons of age 15 years and above was stable at 46.8 % in April-June, 2026 compared to 46.9% in January-March, 2026. In urban areas, the male WPR increased marginally to 70.7% in the current quarter from 70.6% in the previous quarter, whereas the urban female WPR stood at 22.8%, compared to 23.1% in the preceding quarter. The overall WPR recorded a decline of 0.3 percentage points, from April–June, 2025 to April–June, 2026. The male WPR remained nearly unchanged during this period, while the female WPR was estimated at 31.3% in April–June, 2026, as against 31.6% in April–June, 2025. Urban WPR for persons of age15 years and above stable at 46.8% in April-June, 2026 • Overall Unemployment Rate (UR) in urban areas remained stable: Overall UR in urban areas for persons of age 15 years and above remained broadly stable at 6.7 % during the present quarter compared to 6.6% in the previous quarter, while it edged up marginally to 4.8% in the current quarter from 4.3% in the previous quarter, in rural areas. Female urban UR decreased to 8.7% in the current quarter from 9.1% in the last quarter. In comparison to last year, in the same quarter, the UR at the person level in rural areas remained at the same level as in the present quarter (4.8%). The UR for rural male decreased to 4.8% in April-June, 2026 from 5.0% in April-June, 2025. In urban areas, the quarter-to-quarter comparison with the previous year shows stability for male and person-level UR, whereas the female UR decreased to 8.7% from 8.9%. Urban UR (age 15+ years) showed broad stability at 6.7%. Regular wage/salaried employees witnessed a rise: In rural and urban areas, engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment showed an upward movement. In rural areas, it increased to 16.1% during April-June, 2026 from 15.5% of the previous quarter, whereas in urban areas it increased to 49.3% from 48.9% during the same period. A quarter-to-quarter comparison with the same period of the previous year also indicates increased engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment from 15.4% in April-June, 2025 to 16.1% in April-June, 2026 in rural areas. In urban areas, the engagement of workers in regular wage/salaried employment remained almost at the same level (49.4% vs 49.3%) during the period.
Regular wage/salaried employees increased in both rural and urban areas in April-June, 2026 quarter in comparison to previous quarter
Increase in employment in both secondary and tertiary sector in rural areas: Employment distribution over sector continues to follow a similar structure, with the rural workforce predominantly engaged in the primary sector and the urban workforce concentrated in the tertiary sector. In rural areas, the share of workers engaged in agriculture stood at 52.9% during April - June 2026, declined from 55.8% in the previous quarter, whereas the share of employment in the tertiary sector increased from 21.7% in January - March, 2026 to 22.7% in the current quarter. The secondary sector, along with mining and quarrying, in rural areas also witnessed a rise from 22.6% in the previous quarter to 24.4% in the current quarter. In urban areas, the share of employment in the tertiary sector remained broadly stable compared to the previous quarter. The share of employment increased to 31.9% in the secondary sector along with mining and quarrying, while the agriculture sector observed a decrease to 6.1% in urban areas.
In comparison to the same quarter of the previous year, engagement in the tertiary sector increased from 22.1% in April-June, 2025 to 22.7% in April-June, 2026 in rural areas. In urban areas, engagement in the tertiary sector increased from 61.7% to 62.0% during the same period.
In rural areas worker engagement in secondary sector increased to 24.4% in April-June, 2026 from 22.6% in previous quarter.
Using the projected population figures of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), the absolute number of workers aged 15 years and above has been estimated. On average, 56.6 crore persons aged 15 years and above were employed in the country during the quarter April-June, 2026, of which 40.2 crore were male and 16.4 crore were female.
Persons surveyed in urban areas 2,40,881
Persons surveyed in rural areas 3,18,792
At the all-India level, the quarterly estimates are based on information collected from a total of 5,59,673 persons surveyed.
The Quarterly Bulletin for the quarter April-June, 2026 is available on the website of the Ministry ( https://www.mospi.gov.in ). Scan the QR code to access the Publications/ Reports

enrichment.summary: MoSPI's NSO released the PLFS Quarterly Bulletin for April–June 2026, the fifth in the series covering both rural and urban India under the Current Weekly Status framework. Key findings include overall LFPR at 54.6% (down from 55.5% previous quarter), urban UR broadly stable at 6.7%, a marginal rise in urban male LFPR to 75.3%, and an increase in regular wage/salaried employment in both rural (16.1%) and urban (49.3%) areas. Secondary sector employment rose in both rural and urban areas, while rural tertiary sector employment also increased. The survey covered 5,59,673 persons and estimated 56.6 crore employed persons aged 15+ nationally.
enrichment.context:
The Periodic Labour Force Survey, conducted by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI, is India's principal high-frequency source for employment-unemployment data, launched in 2017 to replace the less frequent quinquennial employment surveys of the NSSO. It reports indicators like Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), and Unemployment Rate (UR) under both Usual Status and Current Weekly Status (CWS) approaches. From January 2025, the survey methodology was revamped to provide monthly and quarterly estimates for both rural and urban India under CWS (earlier quarterly bulletins covered only urban areas), enabling more granular tracking of labour market dynamics, including sectoral shifts (primary/agriculture, secondary/industry, tertiary/services) and employment status (self-employed, regular wage/salaried, casual labour).

This data is central to policy discourse on jobless growth, informalisation of labour, women's workforce participation, and structural transformation of the economy (shift from agriculture to industry/services). Trends such as rising regular wage employment and secondary sector growth are often cited as indicators of formalisation and industrial job creation, while declining LFPR, especially female LFPR, remains a persistent concern for India's demographic dividend narrative. PLFS estimates also feed into computation of GDP, poverty, and inequality metrics, and are closely watched alongside other labour indicators like EPFO payroll data and CMIE surveys.

prelims_questions.question: The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted by which organization?
options: Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour and Employment
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that PLFS is conducted by the NSO under the Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI).

prelims_questions.question: With reference to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), consider the following statements: 1. The Current Weekly Status (CWS) framework provides quarterly labour force estimates for both rural and urban India since April-June 2025. 2. Prior to the revamp effective January 2025, PLFS Quarterly Bulletins presented labour market indicators only for urban areas. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that earlier Quarterly Bulletins (up to December 2024) covered only urban areas, and the April-June 2025 bulletin was the first to cover both rural and urban areas under CWS, confirming both statements as correct.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the revamped Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) methodology in providing a more comprehensive picture of India's labour market. How do indicators like LFPR, WPR, and UR help in formulating employment policy?

Analyze the trends in sectoral employment shifts (primary, secondary, tertiary) as reflected in recent PLFS data. What do these trends indicate about the structural transformation of the Indian economy?
